Actual Bioconductor submission baseline

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

The submission baseline is 21f9ea098b69c444a884a49bc254de711968e3b5, submitted August 31, 2026. It is not the later internal-refactor baseline. The original official run used BiocCheck 1.49.30, Bioconductor 3.24 and R 4.6.1, and reported 0 errors, 1 warning, 3 notes.

The authoritative chain is:

  1. Submission issue 176 records the initial clone, first build and authors’ diagnostic explanation.
  2. First source build explicitly resets to the submitted commit.
  3. Original Bioconductor check supplies the preserved official/00BiocCheck.log and official/output.log.
  4. official/sceptre_0.99.0.tar.gz is the original hosted source artifact, SHA256 5300b3e3adfbb73a9a2173384ea3ec7e57b8cad8612f3fdc8116d5db5156eaf4. Its RemoteSha identifies the submitted commit. The 75 checked packaged R, native, man, vignette and NAMESPACE files match Git exactly. DESCRIPTION differs only through build-time wrapping and R-universe metadata.

The live Compass preflight searched sceptre Bioconductor and sceptre submission, then read the exact projects/Bioconductor submission.md note. That note identifies issue 176 and the local planning tracker. Its historical tracker says five notes; the actual submitted official build and authors’ September 1 issue comment say three. The official build is primary. No Compass content was changed.

Matched checker runs

The two local runs preserve separate process logs, complete checker logs, serialized/JSON result objects, session details and commands in matched-1.47.26/ and matched-1.49.30/. They use the exact official wrapper options no-check-R-ver and no-check-bioc-help; no coding, formatting, documentation or dependency check is disabled. The original wrapper is pinned to r-universe action commit e859fe2adc2553a5c8b0b2ec6044215d60d3d9c7.

BiocCheck 1.49.30 was installed into an isolated temporary library from official source commit ca5c23e019dd695b7a5e29286f593a0e9b13639a; its source archive, DESCRIPTION and install log are retained in checker-1.49.30/. No user library was modified. The original hosted R/Linux environment was not recreated; the local checker’s version and flags match, while platform/dependency differences remain explicit. Candidate qualification must use the same isolated library.

An independent audit also ran the unchanged submitted archive under 1.47.26 with all default checks enabled. That run reported 1 error, 1 warning, 5 notes, including a support-site HTTP timeout and the unchanged R-minimum and mailing-list notes. Its exact invocation, terminal log, complete diagnostic JSON and result are retained in external-audit/unsuppressed-1.47.26/. This is not a clean unsuppressed check. The official-wrapper comparison above retains the original submission’s two documented options; it must not be presented as all default checks passing. The independent authority/fix-scope reports are preserved verbatim under external-audit/ with their original manifest.

The 1.47.26 function-length checker overwrites duplicate function names. The 1.49.30 checker retains both compute_group methods and flags the inherited 52-line StatQqBand method, explaining the one-function difference. Inventory scripts preserve duplicate entries by index.

Diagnostic instances, not just categories

The existing warning is absence of a direct Bioconductor dependency. The authors justified it in the September 1 issue comment; it is not a new warning from this refactor and no meaningless dependency is added to silence it.

The original display note covers eight cat() calls in the S4 print(sceptre_object) method and one print() used to serialize the summary under sink(). inventories/display-call-lineage.csv maps each original call to the pre-cleanup qualified source. The summary call moved from R/s4_analysis_functs_2.R:723 into R/output_resources.R:18; cleanup added connection/sink restoration without creating a new logging use. This is inherited functional lineage, not an additional diagnostic instance.

The original long-function note has complete inventories for both checkers. inventories/qualified-long-function-lineage.csv compares the pre-cleanup qualified archive from source 169c16e with the submitted source. It records explicit rename/move evidence, so renamed permutation/CRT workers and the S4 print method are not counted as new merely because their names/lines moved. Under 1.47.26 the 69 current sites comprise 44 inherited sites, 22 new sites and 3 new threshold crossings. The latter are the formula builder (47 to 52), backed object reader (39 to 63), and show method (50 to 54). Extracting a new long helper from an old long body is still classified as a new site. Semantic lineage does not assert AST identity or excuse new behavior within a function.

The pre-cleanup archive has 473 long lines: 110 exact unchanged submitted line instances and 363 new or modified instances. The complete source-text inventory and conservative exact-text delta are in inventories/. A lower total or an old formatting-note category alone would not establish a clean delta.

The following pre-cleanup diagnostics were absent from both matched baseline runs and must be resolved:

  • 1:3 in R/distributed_execution.R at lines 290 and 343.
  • Paste inside the progress-message signal in R/execution.R:42.
  • Three superassignments: R/perturbation_fits.R:51 and R/schema_migration.R:389,393.
  • Missing runnable examples for prepare_execution, execute_work_unit, and collect_execution.
  • New or newly long functions and new/modified overlong lines described above.

Line references in this section intentionally identify the frozen pre-cleanup source. The final candidate comparison below records the actual cleanup result.

review-helpers.R and its log preserve an independent review of the structural helper extraction against the frozen pre-cleanup source: 40 exact comparisons passed across low-MOI complement/NT permutation and high-MOI complement CRT, including stage identities, plans, ordered contexts, unit values, collection, RNG/caller immutability and representative failure messages. This comparison loads functions in isolated environments over the same pre-cleanup installed class/runtime. It does not replace final frozen-source installed validation.

Frozen cleanup comparison

Implementation commit 01bb39ccf8373ae8965a2679ee4813a63ea2d85d produced archive SHA256 606363fce32238354fc0d126d79f515973da7c8287ca43b14ce53ce2d00df4b7. BiocCheck 1.49.30 on that exact archive completed with 0 errors, 1 warning, 3 notes, using the original official wrapper options and the same local checker environment as the matched original-source baseline.

The remaining warning is the original dependency warning. All nine flagged display/serialization calls map to the original submitted sites. The remaining 45 long functions map to already flagged submission functions; the remaining 108 long lines reuse exact submitted source text, with multiplicity preserved. There are zero new flagged function sites and zero new or modified long lines, as well as no new diagnostic categories. The literal sequence, condition-paste, superassignment and missing-example notes are absent.

Complete candidate receipts and every remaining instance’s original source location are in ../submission-cleanup/qualification/remaining-diagnostic-map.json, instance-gate/ and bioccheck-1.49.30/. The source helper comparison was repeated against this exact frozen archive; all 40 comparisons passed. Final installed tests, executable examples, historical scientific parity and R CMD check have separate integration-owner receipts and are not inferred from BiocCheck success.

baseline.json records source/runtime scope. files-sha256.json pins captured artifacts without rewriting their bytes. The original submission archive and checker source are historical evidence and must remain separate from any new candidate archive.
